# PR #4323: Patch: the dev dashboard's audit reads a time range

Closes #4298

## What changed

`GET /api/admin/audit` accepts optional `since`/`until` query bounds (epoch milliseconds, inclusive on the row's `at`), composed with the existing `profile_id`/`route` filters and `before_id` paging. The dashboard's audit page exposes them as Since/Until date-time inputs next to the existing filters; Clear resets them and Older stays inside the window.

- `crates/server/src/admin/store.rs`: `AdminActionFilter` gains `since`/`until`; pg `actions_page` bounds `at` with `to_timestamp($n::double precision / 1000.0)` (same conversion as `posts_standing`), fake filters on `row.at`. Order stays `(at desc, id desc)`; page size unchanged.
- `crates/server/src/api/admin.rs`: `get_audit` parses both bounds (blank means none, like `query_trimmed`), 400s `"since must be a whole number"`, `"until must be a whole number"`, and `"since must not be after until"`, matching the existing `before_id` style. Docs updated.
- `apps/admin`: `api.audit()` sends both params; `Audit.tsx` adds the two inputs, an applied window, and a `toMs` (`datetime-local` → epoch ms) helper; `testids.ts` gains `auditSince`/`auditUntil`.
- Spec: one added sentence each in `spec/14-economy.md` §14.10 and `spec/rulings/R3074000.md`. No new ruling, no `spec/pending/` file, no `spec index` run.

## Tests

New: `audit_pages_by_since_and_until` (store contract — middle/point/one-sided/empty windows, composition with `profile_id`/`route`/`before_id`, shared-`at` tie-break, in-window paging with no gaps/repeats), `audit_read_filters_by_since_and_until` (API — window reads, composed filters, in-window paging, blank-as-none, all three 400s), two `audit()` wire CASES in `api.test.ts`, and three Audit tests in `Dashboard.test.tsx` (Apply sends window and replaces list, Clear empties it, Older keeps it).

Results, all observed: store contract `dev_dashboard` 12/12 on both `memory` and `postgres` harnesses (fake and Postgres agree); API `api::admin::` 18/18, re-run after the final edit; admin `api.test.ts` 30/30, `Dashboard.test.tsx` 30/30, admin `typecheck` clean; `cargo fmt --check` clean; `cargo clippy -p jackioh-server --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean; `cargo jackioh spec check`: 2310 rulings, 5812 proofs ok.

## Decisions the issue did not settle

- The API test seeds rows through the store with pinned `at` values rather than HTTP writes: three in-process writes share a millisecond, so a middle-window assertion off HTTP writes would be flaky. Rejected alternative: sleeping between writes.
- Dashboard tests compute expected params via `Date.parse` of the typed string, so they hold in any browser timezone; only the epoch-ms wire format is pinned, never the widget's zone.
- A `read` closure for the API test failed borrowck (a closure can't return a future borrowing its arg), so the `expect` calls are written out. Clippy's `collapsible_if` on the `since > until` guard became a let-chain.

## Reviewer notes

The pg predicate binds `Option<i64>` to `$n::double precision` parameters, mirroring the existing `actions_append`/`posts_standing` `to_timestamp($n::double precision / 1000.0)` pattern. `before_id` remains the stable id-based paging cursor; the window only bounds `at`, so concurrent-write timestamp/id skew can't duplicate or skip rows.

### Its own review

Built and checked on `muse`. This is a draft while its own review run, on the same subscription, reviews it adversarially and fixes what it finds (up to 3 rounds); CI runs on it meanwhile. Once that review approves it, it is marked ready and auto-merge turns on.

| catalog (`cargo jackioh catalog check`) | pass | 1s |

# #4298: Patch: the dev dashboard's audit reads a time range
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means
The dev dashboard has a page listing every admin and dev-tool action ever taken: who did it, which button they pressed, and what changed. Today you can only filter that list by account and by action name, and you page backwards from the newest entry. Once this is built, you can also ask for just one window of time, such as everything from last Tuesday, which turns a long trawl into one lookup. A maintainer tracking down who changed what and when notices; players notice nothing.

## Why
Every write of every dev and admin route appends one row to `admin_actions` (R3074000), and that table only grows: ratings, news posts and take-downs, plus every dev-tool write (XP, Jlore, fills, clears, quest tools). The read side, however, has stood still since it was built: `GET /api/admin/audit` filters only by exact account and exact route with cursor paging, and the dashboard page exposes only those two text boxes. There is no way to ask the natural incident question ("what did anyone do between 2am and 4am?") short of paging through everything newer. No open or closed issue covers audit time filtering (the audit page and its who/what filters shipped under #4168/#4183, now closed).

## Proposal
Add optional `since`/`until` (epoch milliseconds, matching the row's `at` field) to `GET /api/admin/audit` as range bounds on the row id's timestamp, expose them as two date-time inputs on the dashboard's audit page next to the existing filters, and keep everything else unchanged: same page size, same newest-first order, same cursor paging composed with the range. Rejected: relative shortcuts ("last 24h") instead of explicit inputs — explicit bounds compose with the existing cursor and are trivially testable; shortcuts can follow if maintainers want them.

## Where it lands
- `crates/server/src/api/admin.rs` (`get_audit`, `AdminActionFilter`)
- Store: the `admin_actions_page` query in `crates/server/src/db/` (fake and Postgres together, plus the contract test in `crates/server/tests/store/contract.rs`)
- `apps/admin/src/Audit.tsx` (and `api.ts`, `testids.ts`) for the two inputs
- SPEC §9.1 / R3074000 (the audit paragraph lives there; the change narrows reads, not what is recorded, so the ruling text needs at most a sentence, not a new ruling)

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `GET /api/admin/audit?since=&until=` returns only rows in the window, combined with the existing `profile_id`/`route` filters and `before_id` paging
- [ ] Bad bounds (non-numbers, `since` after `until`) are 400 with a sentence, like the existing `before_id` validation
- [ ] The dashboard page offers both bounds, clears them with Clear, and keeps paging inside the window
- [ ] Fake and Postgres agree (contract test), since the Docker suites are the only place RLS/trigger behavior is checked
- [ ] `cargo test -p jackioh-server` (incl. the store contract) and the admin app tests pass

## Size and risks
Small: one bounded range predicate, two inputs, tests on both sides. Risk: timestamp-vs-id ordering edge cases under concurrent writes — mitigated by bounding on the row timestamp while keeping `before_id` as the stable paging cursor, and by asserting newest-first order inside a window in the contract test. Rejected alternative: full-text search over the request/before/after JSON — heavier (needs `pg_trgm` or equivalent, new indexes) for a question time bounds already answer.

2. Register the name in the `both_stores!` list at line 13046.

Add a `toMs` helper (trim; empty yields `undefined`; else `Date.parse`, with `NaN` yielding `undefined`). Render two `<input type="datetime-local">` controls with `Since`/`Until` labels and the new testids next to the existing filters. - `crates/server/tests/store/contract.rs`: new `audit_pages_by_since_and_until` asserts window filtering, combination with `profile_id`/`route`/`before_id`, newest-first order inside the window (including the shared-`at` tie-break), and the empty window. Run `cargo test -p jackioh-server --test server_store dev_dashboard`.
- `crates/server/tests/api/admin.rs`: new `audit_read_filters_by_since_and_until` asserts window reads, composed filters, in-window paging, and the three 400 cases. Run `cargo test -p jackioh-server --test server api::admin::`.
- `apps/admin/src/api.test.ts`: add `CASES` rows: `audit` with `{ since, until }` sends `/api/admin/audit?since=…&until=…`, and window params combined with `beforeId`/`profileId`/`route`; blanks still omitted. Run `pnpm --dir apps/admin test src/api.test.ts`.
- `apps/admin/src/Dashboard.test.tsx`, `describe("Audit")`: add "Apply sends the time window and replaces the list" (type into the Since/Until inputs, Apply, expect the windowed URL sent once and rows replaced), "Clear empties the time window too" (inputs cleared, unfiltered read re-sent), and "Older keeps the time window" (Older request carries `before_id` plus the window params). Run `pnpm --dir apps/admin test src/Dashboard.test.tsx`.
- Checks: `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -p jackioh-server --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo jackioh spec check`.

## Done when

- [ ] `GET /api/admin/audit?since=&until=` returns only rows with `since <= at <= until`, combined with `profile_id`/`route` and `before_id` paging; page size and newest-first order unchanged.
- [ ] Non-numeric `since`/`until` and `since` after `until` are 400 with a sentence.
- [ ] The audit page shows Since and Until inputs, Clear resets them, and Older stays inside the window.
- [ ] The contract test passes on both stores (Postgres half runs in the Docker suite).
- [ ] `cargo test -p jackioh-server` (both test targets above), the two admin app test files, fmt, clippy, and `cargo jackioh spec check` all pass.

## Risks

- Timestamp-vs-id skew under concurrent writes: two rows can share an `at` with `id`s in either order. Mitigation, already in the design: the window bounds only `at`, while `before_id` stays the stable id-based paging cursor and ordering stays `(at desc, id desc)` in both stores; the contract test locks the shared-`at` tie-break and in-window paging.
- Fake/Postgres drift: both implementations change in the same step and the same contract test runs against both; the Docker suite is the only place RLS/trigger behavior is checked, and this change adds no migration so those invariants are untouched.
- No hidden-information or client-enforcement risk: the audit stays dev-only behind `admin_caller`, and the client only forwards typed input (CLAUDE.md rule 7).
- `datetime-local` parses in the browser's local zone while rows are epoch ms; acceptable for a dev tool, and tests pin the wire format (epoch-ms integers), not the widget's zone.

None.
